title: Frobenius acts on roots of unity by the q-th power
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime, and $k$ an algebraic closure of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; let $\varphi_q\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, $z\mapsto z^q$, be the arithmetic Frobenius and $\gamma=\varphi_q^{-1}$ the geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-substitution]. Let $N\geq1$ be an integer prime to $p$ and $\mu_N(k)=\{\zeta\in k^\times:\zeta^N=1\}$. Then:

1. $\mu_N(k)$ is a cyclic group of order $N$, and every automorphism $\sigma$ of the field $k$ maps $\mu_N(k)$ to itself.
2. $\varphi_q(\zeta)=\zeta^q$ and $\gamma(\zeta)=\zeta^{q'}$ for every $\zeta\in\mu_N(k)$, where $q'\in\mathbf Z$ is any integer with $qq'\equiv1\pmod N$ (it exists since $\gcd(q,N)=1$).
3. Let $\ell\neq p$ be a prime and $T_\ell\mu(k)=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$, the limit along the maps $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$. It is a free $\mathbf Z_\ell$-module of rank one [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] (written additively), $\varphi_q$ and $\gamma$ act on it componentwise, and $\varphi_q$ acts as multiplication by $q\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$ and $\gamma$ as multiplication by $q^{-1}\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$.

source.place: (2.2), p. 281: 'si k = F_q, la substitution de Frobenius phi : x -> x^q agit [sur Q_l(1)] par multiplication par q'; the geometric Frobenius F = phi^{-1}: literature/deligne-weil-II_PMIHES-1980-52.pdf, (1.1.7), pp. 150-151

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-primitive-root] with n=N to the algebraically closed field k. Since N is prime to p=char(k), it gives exactly N distinct roots and a primitive root, hence the multiplicative group μ_N(k) is cyclic of order N. For any field automorphism σ, σ(ζ)^N=σ(ζ^N)=1, so σ preserves μ_N(k); this last preservation is the direct field-homomorphism calculation. Applying the same equation to σ^{-1} shows that the image is the whole subgroup.

source.place: first paragraph: arithmetic Frobenius sends each root of unity to its q-th power

proof.text: By [def-weil-frobenius-substitution], the arithmetic Frobenius is the field automorphism φ_q(z)=z^q and the geometric Frobenius is φ_q^{-1}. Thus φ_q(ζ)=ζ^q. Since gcd(q,N)=1, choose q′ with qq′≡1 mod N; then φ_q(ζ^{q′})=ζ, and applying φ_q^{-1} gives γ(ζ)=ζ^{q′}. If q′ is replaced by another inverse, the two exponents differ by a multiple of N and give the same value on μ_N(k).

source.place: second paragraph: inverse of q modulo each ℓ^n and the inverse automorphism

proof.text: Regard k^× as the additive group M=Additive(k^×). Its ℓ-torsion is the subgroup of units ζ with ζ^ℓ=1, which is μ_ℓ(k); by [lem-sc-primitive-root] this has cardinality ℓ. Multiplication by ℓ on M is surjective: for x∈k^×, the polynomial X^ℓ−x has a root y in the algebraically closed field k by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and y is nonzero with y^ℓ=x. Therefore [lem-av-tate-module-group-rank] with r=1 gives a ℤ_ℓ-linear equivalence T_ℓM≃ℤ_ℓ. Under [def-tate-module-abelian-group], this T_ℓM is exactly the inverse limit of the groups μ_{ℓ^r}(k) with transition ζ↦ζ^ℓ, so it is the stated free rank-one module.

source.place: slopmaster2 read-only source, theorem AddCommGroup.tateModule.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_natCard_eq, lines 228–230: specialize to M=Additive(k^×) and r=1; divisibility and torsion-cardinality hypotheses verified explicitly in this step

proof.text: The action on T_ℓM is componentwise by [def-tate-module-abelian-group]. It preserves the transition maps because for s=φ_q or γ one has s(ζ^ℓ)=s(ζ)^ℓ. For r≥1, apply Step 2 with N=ℓ^r: the r-th coordinate φ_q(ζ)=ζ^q is q-fold addition in Additive(k^×), hence the action of q modulo ℓ^r by the scalar rule of the cited definition. Thus φ_q is multiplication by q∈ℤ_ℓ. Choose the unique inverse residue c_r of q modulo ℓ^r, which exists since ℓ≠p and q=p^a. The reduction of c_{r+1} is an inverse of q modulo ℓ^r, so uniqueness gives its equality to c_r. Hence c=(c_r)∈ℤ_ℓ and qc=1 in every coordinate, making q a unit with inverse c=q^{-1}. Step 2 gives γ(ζ)=ζ^{c_r} on μ_{ℓ^r}(k), so the scalar rule identifies its componentwise action with multiplication by c. If the limit includes r=0, that coordinate is μ_1(k)={1} and satisfies both formulas automatically.

source.place: second paragraph: compatible inverses define q^{-1} in ℤ_ℓ and the inverse automorphism acts by q^{-1}

split_report.summary: Audited the imported three-clause statement against Deligne Weil I (2.2), Weil II (1.1.7), and the current cyclotomic blueprint. No single sorry-free project declaration states all three clauses. The proof now uses the existing primitive-root statement and the closed general Tate-module rank theorem; it spells out the algebraic-closure divisibility, torsion-cardinality, componentwise scalar action, and inverse-exponent calculation. No new node was created because each auxiliary fact is already an existing definition or lemma, and the only rank theorem is the reusable existing group-theoretic node.
